chain.label: Vaguely worded NOTAM prohibiting the ASE approach at night, never delivered to the ASE tower
chain.trigger: The NOTAM stated, 'circling NA [not authorized] at night,' but the intended meaning of the NOTAM was to prohibit the entire instrument approach procedure at night.

chain.label: Operational pressure to land at ASE: 41-minute late departure, 1858 noise curfew, irate charter customer, customer on the jumpseat
chain.trigger: The flight crew was dealing with various sources of operational pressure during the accident flight. These sources were the airplane's late departure from LAX, the ASE nighttime landing curfew, and the charter customer's strong desire to land at ASE.

chain.label: Darkness at the approach path well before official night because of terrain shadowing
chain.trigger: the Safety Board calculated that the sun had set below the mountainous terrain about 25 minutes before the official sunset time and that evening civil twilight ended about 1830 rather than 1855

chain.label: ASE surrounded by high, unlighted terrain with the final approach over rising ground
chain.trigger: The airport is located about 3 miles northwest of the city of Aspen at an elevation of 7,815 feet msl and is surrounded on all sides by high terrain.

chain.label: Deteriorating visibility in light snow showers along the approach course; three preceding aircraft missed the approach
chain.trigger: the controller informed all airplanes on frequency that the visibility north of the airport was 2 miles ... 'the weather's gone down they're not making it in'

chain.label: Incomplete approach briefing, omitted required approach callouts, and no challenge by the first officer
chain.trigger: the captain did not discuss the instrument approach procedure during his approach briefing, as required by the Avjet Operations Manual ... did not brief the missed approach procedure

caused_by.evidence: The captain did not discuss the instrument approach procedure, the missed approach procedure, and other required elements during his approach briefing because he expected to execute a visual approach to the airport.

chain.label: Crew continued the approach instead of diverting despite missed approach reports and worsening weather (plan continuation)
chain.trigger: the flight crew focused on cues that supported the goal of landing at ASE ... the crew did not adequately consider information that supported a change of plans

caused_by.evidence: The operational pressure on the flight crew probably resulted in the crew's intent to continue with its original plan to land at ASE.

The three reports of missed approaches and the deteriorating visibility to the north should have alerted the flight crewmembers that they might also need to execute a missed approach because of the weather. However, the CVR did not record any discussion between the crewmembers at this point regarding a possible missed approach.

According to the intent of the NOTAM, the instrument approach procedure to ASE was not authorized after 1855. As a result, the flight crew should not have been attempting this procedure to the airport.
the flight crew was not adequately prepared to perform ASE's instrument and missed approach procedures

chain.label: Descent below step-down fix altitudes and below the MDA without the required visual reference
chain.trigger: The airplane passed the step-down fix located 9.5 DME south of the Red Table VOR about 1901:00 at an altitude of 9,500 feet, 900 feet below the specified minimum altitude

caused_by.evidence: the captain continued flight below the authorized MDA after failing to establish or maintain visual contact with the runway

The CVR did not record any announcement by the first officer that the airplane was 300 feet below the minimum step-down altitude of 10,400 feet ... the first officer did not verbally challenge the captain

chain.label: Spoilers deployed with gear down and full flaps and power reduced to 55 percent N2, sustaining a 2,200 fpm descent
chain.trigger: The captain likely extended the spoilers and reduced engine power to increase the airplane's rate of descent to get below the snow showers and visually acquire the runway. However, these actions were contrary to spoiler information in the Gulfstream GIII Flight Manual

caused_by.evidence: extended the spoilers and reduced engine power to increase the airplane's rate of descent to get below the snow showers and visually acquire the runway
the flight crewmembers initially tried to establish and maintain contact with ground references so that they would be able to fly visually to the airport

chain.label: Crew never established or maintained visual contact with the runway environment while flying visually
chain.trigger: About the same time as the airplane passed the missed approach point, the captain asked, 'where's it at?' This statement suggests that the captain had not identified, or had lost visual contact with, the runway.

caused_by.evidence: the dark conditions would have significantly degraded the flight crew's ability to see and safely avoid terrain while making the visual transition from the instrument approach to an intended landing
The reduced visibility and light snow showers near the airport would have further degraded the flight crew's ability to see and safely avoid the terrain.
areas of unlighted terrain conflicted with traffic patterns and circling descent maneuvers near the airport

chain.label: Airplane arrived over rising terrain at 485 feet above field elevation, right of centerline, with GPWS sink rate alerts
chain.trigger: The airplane passed the missed approach point about 1901:36 at an altitude of about 8,300 feet, 485 feet above field elevation rather than the specified 2,385 feet above field elevation

caused_by.evidence: The flight crew crossed step-down fixes below the minimum specified altitudes ... descended below the minimum descent altitude (MDA)
the airplane maintained a descent rate of about 2,200 feet per minute and an airspeed of about 125 knots
The airplane crashed into sloping terrain about 2,400 feet short of the runway threshold.

chain.label: Abrupt steep left bank exceeding 40 degrees at about 100 feet above the terrain
chain.trigger: About 1901:57, the CVR recorded the GPWS bank angle alert when the airplane was banked about 40º left wing down.

caused_by.evidence: It is possible that the captain saw the runway or the highway and was making a steep turn to align the airplane with the runway without a substantial overshoot. It is also possible that the captain was starting to see terrain that had been obscured by the darkness and the weather conditions and was banking the airplane to avoid the terrain.

chain.label: Stick shaker activation as airspeed fell below the stall speed for the bank angle
chain.trigger: Calculated airspeeds between 1901:52 and 1901:57 ranged from 120 to 127 knots. At 40º of bank and the airplane's weight at the time of the accident, the stall speed was about 134 knots.

caused_by.evidence: Spectrograms of the two stick shaker systems from the test airplane's CAM channel recording contained characteristics similar to the rumbling noise on the accident airplane's recording.

chain.label: Left wing tip struck sloping terrain 2,400 feet short of the runway 15 threshold; airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The airplane crashed into terrain while in a steep left bank about 2,400 feet short of the runway 15 threshold, 300 feet to the right (west) of the runway centerline

caused_by.evidence: the airplane initially impacted terrain in a 49º left-wing-down attitude, with a flightpath angle of -15º
the terrain rose again as the airplane crossed the riverbed ... the terrain rose another 25 feet (the elevation of the accident site)
a rumbling noise began about 1901:52, blended into the background about 1901:57, and continued until the end of the recording

chain.label: All 18 occupants fatally injured
chain.trigger: All of the passengers and crewmembers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed.

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable for any of the airplane occupants because they were subjected to impact forces that exceeded the limits of human tolerance.
